candidate_relations.reason: The benchmark requires disseminated Strongyloides infection with concurrent Aspergillus infection, supported by stool ova/parasite positivity, bronchoscopy revealing Strongyloides filariform larvae, BAL positive for Aspergillus, elevated beta-D-glucan, and cavitary/tree-in-bud lung lesions. C001 attributes the GI symptoms to CKD-associated dysmotility, ignoring the confirmed parasitic and fungal infections entirely and representing a completely different diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: CKD-associated intestinal dysmotility is a functional GI diagnosis unrelated to the infectious etiology required by the benchmark

case_quality_flags: Classic hyperinfection syndrome setting: immunosuppression with cyclophosphamide and high-dose corticosteroids in a patient with CKD facilitating Strongyloides dissemination
Dual infection (Strongyloides + Aspergillus) confirmed by direct microbiological evidence from bronchoscopy and BAL
Only one candidate provided, which is clearly not equivalent to the reference diagnosis
